common_name: Middle Triassic Sea-Lily Crinoid (Stereom Gyroid Ossicles)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Encrinus liliiformis (12 nm, detail scale)

paleobiology.note: The Encrinus chronoseries in this campaign has a single dated slot. Predecessor and successor are the neighboring crinoid grades used to say what is special at 240 Ma.

equations: du/dt = a - u + u^2 v + D_u laplacian(u)
dv/dt = b - u^2 v + D_v laplacian(v)
k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
governing_law.boundary_conditions: Periodic transect for the numerical control; Neumann disk for the radial m=0 mode used in the render.

parameters_this_scale.note: Not the 612 nm sibling parameters. a, b and delta are specific to the 12 nm Muschelkalk end-member.

chronoseries_comparison.name: Holocrinus dubius
chronoseries_comparison.what_changes: Longer occlusion wavelength and a lower inhibitor ratio. Recovery-fauna labyrinthic stereom, before the Muschelkalk galleried mesh.

chronoseries_comparison.name: Encrinus liliiformis
chronoseries_comparison.what_changes: Short-wavelength minimum. Highest delta of the three-point series. One 12 nm wavelength inside a disk of radius about 10.4 nm, i.e. a sub-region of a ~100 nm calcite nanograin.

chronoseries_comparison.name: Chelocrinus cassianus
chronoseries_comparison.what_changes: Wavelength rebounds and delta falls as the Muschelkalk high-magnesium regime ends.

empirical_claims: Turing 1952 and Schnakenberg 1979 supply the dispersion relation and the two-species kinetics. They do not mention Encrinus.

Stolarski, Gorzelak, Mazur, Marrocchi and Meibom 2009 measured crinoid stereom nanograins of about 100 nm with gaps of a few nanometres, on Jurassic isocrinid columnals, not on a 12 nm TEM of Encrinus.
The 12 nm figure is this slot's assigned detail scale, placed inside that measured nanograin window.

The radial luminance of the project stereom-gyroid rendering is fit in-sample by four harmonics of one fundamental (Pearson r = 0.9996, RMSE = 0.0031). That rendering's scale bar reads 100 micrometres.

reported_in_source: Turing dispersion relation and Schnakenberg kinetics, with the onset wavenumber formula.
Crinoid stereom is a nanocrystalline calcite mesh; published nanograin diameters are about 100 nm (Stolarski et al. 2009).
reconstructed_in_script: Diffusivities that place onset k_c at 1.238e-8 m for a=0.047, b=1.153, delta=22.4.
Equal-diffusion ablation, delta sweep, and the 248/240/232 Ma wavelength ordering.
Galerkin fit of the stereom radial profile and the sepia growth animation.
transfer_boundary: Jurassic isocrinid nanograin measurements are transferred as the size window that makes a 12 nm Muschelkalk wavelength meaningful. They are not a measurement of Encrinus liliiformis.
does_not_claim: Does not claim a 12 nm TEM exists for the Ingelfingen slab.
Does not claim the gallery stereom image was acquired at 12 nm.
Does not claim the pixel dark-mask IoU (0.17) is a spatial registration of the fossil.

stereom_target.role: radial microstructure target only; scale bar on the image reads 100 um
